episode.title: bug(core): client-initiated tool calls silently bypass ASK_USER confirmation (scheduler/policy.ts)
episode.before: The scheduler's policy-checking path calls the policy engine and then unconditionally converts PolicyDecision.ASK_USER to PolicyDecision.ALLOW when a tool request is marked isClientInitiated and does not contain additional_permissions. The condition is not restricted by a tool allowlist, approval mode, or an explicit policy opt-in, so client-initiated calls can skip the confirmation prompt. The checkout's scheduler policy test explicitly asserts this behavior for an ASK_USER result.
episode.after: No verified post-fix state exists for issue #29305. The GitHub evidence bundle has no linked pull requests, and the issue was closed as not_planned after an unanswered request for additional information. The pinned ref does not implement this issue: it is a separate #29170 path-boundary and symlink-hardening commit, and its changed-file set does not include scheduler/policy.ts or scheduler/policy.test.ts. The client-initiated ASK_USER-to-ALLOW behavior therefore remains uncorrected in the inspected checkout.
episode.diff: The pinned ref 567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4 has parent 60d35f48a84a32115dc7095f2a59ab47ab467988 and changes 13 files, with 1,029 additions and 64 deletions according to the commit view. Its diff concerns workspace path-boundary enforcement, effective working-directory propagation through shell safety checks, symlink-aware file discovery, sandbox-manager interfaces, and related tests. The implementation adds workspace-aware shell heuristics and passes effective cwd values into command-safety checks; its tests cover escaping the workspace boundary and YOLO-mode behavior. It does not alter the scheduler confirmation bypass described by issue #29305, and no implementation-bearing diff for that issue can be established.

evidence_units.claim: Issue #29305 reports that client-initiated tool calls with a policy result of ASK_USER are silently upgraded to ALLOW when additional_permissions is absent, and expects client-initiated calls to continue honoring ASK_USER unless an explicit allowlist or policy opt-in permits bypassing confirmation.

The issue bundle records issue #29305 as closed with state_reason not_planned; it contains no linked pull requests, and the final timeline comment says the item was closed for lack of requested information after 14 days.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json: issue.state, issue.state_reason, linked_pull_requests, comments, and timeline

evidence_units.claim: The inspected scheduler policy implementation checks for ASK_USER, isClientInitiated, and the absence of args.additional_permissions, then returns ALLOW with the policy rule instead of continuing to the confirmation path.

checkPolicy obtains the decision from the configured PolicyEngine before applying the client-initiated bypass, so the bypass is a scheduler-layer post-processing change rather than a policy-engine allowlist decision.

The scheduler policy test named 'should return ALLOW if decision is ASK_USER and request is client-initiated' supplies an ASK_USER policy result and a client-initiated request with empty args, then expects ALLOW. This test validates the reported bypass rather than the issue's requested safe behavior.

The pinned ref has subject 'fix(core): enhance workspace path boundary checks and symlink resolution in command safety and file discovery (#29170)' and parent 60d35f48a84a32115dc7095f2a59ab47ab467988; its subject identifies issue #29170, not issue #29305.
evidence_units.source: git cat-file -p 567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4 and git log --no-walk in the checkout; https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/commit/567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4

evidence_units.claim: Comparing the pinned commit tree with its parent shows modifications only in policy-engine, sandbox command-safety and sandbox-manager code/tests, file-discovery code/tests, and tools/ls.ts. The changed set contains no packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.ts and no packages/core/src/scheduler/policy.test.ts.
evidence_units.source: git ls-tree -r comparison of 567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4 and 60d35f48a84a32115dc7095f2a59ab47ab467988 in the checkout

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation extends PolicyEngine shell heuristics with dir_path/effective workspace cwd handling, forces ASK_USER when the effective cwd escapes the workspace outside YOLO mode, and passes the effective cwd to isKnownSafeCommand and isDangerousCommand. This is workspace-boundary enforcement, not client-initiated confirmation handling.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned diff updates PolicyEngine.check call sites to pass shellDirPath into applyShellHeuristics, and updates sandbox-manager command-safety call sites to receive effective cwd values; no scheduler confirmation call site is changed.
evidence_units.source: GitHub commit diff for 567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4, policy-engine.ts and sandbox-manager sections: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/commit/567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4

evidence_units.claim: The pinned ref adds policy-engine tests that require ASK_USER when dir_path escapes the workspace and preserve ALLOW in YOLO mode, along with command-safety and symlink/file-discovery tests; these tests do not exercise isClientInitiated or the scheduler confirmation bypass.
evidence_units.source: GitHub commit diff for 567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4, changed test files and policy-engine.test.ts sections: https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/commit/567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4

unresolved_questions: No linked implementation or merged resolution for issue #29305 can be established from the GitHub evidence bundle; the issue was closed as not_planned rather than resolved by a pull request.

The pinned ref 567afbbe8fc7927e38bd40733bf09cafc227ede4 is the implementation for a different path-boundary/symlink-hardening issue (#29170), despite being mentioned in #29305 only as related recent hardening.

No post-fix validation oracle demonstrates that a client-initiated request receiving ASK_USER remains ASK_USER or is bypassed only through an explicit allowlist or policy opt-in. The available scheduler test instead continues to expect ALLOW for that case.
Because the checkout cannot establish an implementation-bearing change for issue #29305, no training-quality Change Action or Issue Workflow is promoted.
